title: pr-67821-safe-rollback-and-migration-guardrails-for-private-deployments
author: Nia Patel
description: Motivation: Private customers require reliable upgrade and downgrade paths when running Redwood Private in VPC or air-gapped environments. This PR adds a guarded upgrade flow that performs pre-upgrade validation, consistent backups, schema migration checks, and explicit downgrade guards to reduce the risk of irreversible state changes. High-level changes: 1) installer: add 'redwood-upgrade' controller (stateless) that orchestrates preflight, backup, migration, and post-checks; 2) helm: templates and hooks for pre-upgrade backup jobs, migration jobs, and annotated resources that record upgrade metadata; 3) terraform: optional 'upgrade_backup' module to snapshot PVs to S3-compatible storage (MinIO), plus IAM policy examples; 4) migration tooling: add migration manager binary (go) that validates forward and backward migrations, produces reversible SQL for Postgres, and can run dry-run via --plan flag; 5) rollback path: restore hooks for Helm that validate checksum+version and refuse downgrade if irreversible migrations detected; 6) docs and runbooks: upgrade runbook with checklist and automatic rollback troubleshooting section; 7) e2e: new integration tests that run upgrade->downgrade in a KinD-like local environment (fast smoke). Checklist: - [x] Preflight validations for cluster/helm/terraform state - [x] Automatic pre-upgrade backup to configured bucket with retention tagging - [x] Migration manager with dry-run and reversible migration detection - [x] Helm hooks to coordinate job sequencing and mark upgrade metadata - [x] Terraform module and example infra to wire backups to MinIO - [x] Tests and CI integration added - [x] Runbook and release notes updated Known limitations: - DR/long-term retention is out of scope (customer-managed retention recommended) - This PR does not include per-tenant encryption key rotation; KMS integration will be follow-up. Rollout plan: merge to release/v1.18, enable feature gate 'safe_upgrade' on a subset of Dedicated clusters via canary, monitor metrics (upgrade.success, upgrade.rollback) in Redwood Console and SLO toolkit. Related: ENG-4021, ENG-4097, SUP-897.
